cards.explanation: The answer is a resting place. Naomi, Ruth's mother-in-law, asks, “…should I not seek a resting place for you, that it may be well with you?” (Ruth 3:1) Notice she's thinking about how things go for Ruth, not just herself. I've been tucked in a drawer, so a good resting place sounds like a WONDERFUL thing to me.

The answer is relative. Naomi says, “Now is not Boaz, with whose servant girls you have been working, a relative of ours?” (Ruth 3:2) So Boaz is more than the man whose servant girls Ruth has been working with. He's family. That detail is going to matter, friends.

The answer is on the threshing floor. Naomi says, “In fact, tonight he is winnowing barley on the threshing floor.” (Ruth 3:2) Winnowing is how the grain gets separated from the chaff. Naomi knows where Boaz will be AND what he'll be doing, friends.

The answer is False. Naomi tells Ruth, “Therefore wash yourself, put on perfume, and wear your best clothes.” (Ruth 3:3) That's the opposite of just showing up as she is. Wash, perfume, best clothes, in that order.

The answer is after he finishes eating and drinking. Naomi says to go down to the threshing floor, “…but do not let the man know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.” (Ruth 3:3) Timing is part of the plan. Ruth waits until Boaz is done with his meal.
The answer is True. Naomi says that when Ruth lies down, “…he will explain to you what you should do.” (Ruth 3:4) Ruth isn't left to figure out the rest on her own. Boaz is the one who will tell her.
The answer is “I will do everything you say…” That's how Ruth answers Naomi. (Ruth 3:5) No stalling, no side questions. Compare that to me with a to-do list, friends. I'd negotiate with MYSELF first.
The answer is False. Verse 7 says, “Then Ruth went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.” That's quiet, friends. If I tried sneaking in, my gold base would clunk and wake the whole bakery.

The answer is to spread the corner of his garment over her. Ruth, the Moabite who has been gleaning in his fields (Ruth 2:2, 3), says, “Spread the corner of your garment over me…” (Ruth 3:9) She tells Boaz who she is first, then she asks. Ruth knows what she's asking for.

The answer is that he is a kinsman-redeemer. Ruth says, “Spread the corner of your garment over me, for you are a kinsman-redeemer.” (Ruth 3:9) She doesn't hand Boaz a long speech. She names who he is to her family.
The answer is True. Boaz says, “You have shown more kindness now than before…” (Ruth 3:10) Notice he says MORE kindness than before. He remembers what came earlier, and he's saying tonight tops it.

The answer is character. Boaz says, “…all my fellow townspeople know that you are a woman of noble character.” (Ruth 3:11) That's what the whole town knows about her. Good character gets around, friends.
The answer is False. Boaz says, “Yes, it is true that I am a kinsman-redeemer, but there is a redeemer nearer than I.” (Ruth 3:12) He doesn't hide that from her. Somebody else is nearer than he is.

The answer is that he will redeem her himself. Boaz says, “But if he does not want to redeem you, as surely as the LORD lives, I will.” (Ruth 3:13) He ties his word to the LORD's name. That's a serious promise.

The answer is False. Boaz says, “Do not let it be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.” (Ruth 3:14) He wants it kept quiet. Meanwhile I can't keep a batch of cookies quiet for ten minutes, because the smell tells on me.

The answer is barley. The text says, “…he poured in six measures of barley and placed it on her.” (Ruth 3:15) Barley is also what Boaz was winnowing on the threshing floor. The text even gives the count: six measures.

The answer is “Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.” Ruth tells Naomi, “He gave me these six measures of barley, for he said, ‘Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’…” (Ruth 3:17) Boaz is thinking of Naomi too. I think Ruth walked home with a full shawl and a full heart.

The answer is that Boaz will not rest until it is settled today. Naomi says, “Wait, my daughter, until you find out how things go, for he will not rest unless he has resolved the matter today.” (Ruth 3:18) Naomi expects Boaz to settle it today. So she tells Ruth to wait.
